title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Hobby Magazine Build Report. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Hobby Magazine Build Report
options.lineage: Japanese model-kit magazines (Hobby Japan, Model Graphix, Dengeki Hobby) and their build-report features
options.thesis: Every project is written up the way a model magazine reports a build: kit, parts used, techniques, finish.
materials: flat process-ink color fields on cool coated paper
boxed spec panels and technique sidebars
options.viewport: Opener spread: a huge condensed headline, a cut-out photo of the featured build (Notifly on a phone or the homelab rig) on a cobalt field, and a kit spec box holding the working Email action.
options.risk: Can tip into a Gunpla fan page and drown the engineer you asked to lead; the hobby stays in the interests spread, and the builds on show are engineering.

raised.raise: Flat ink edge to edge: the feature color owns whole spreads, with no gradients, glass, or glow anywhere.
One color, one job: vermilion appears only on the Email action, never as decoration.
Type scale carries volume: one shouting headline per spread, everything else set calm.
Width as voice: one variable grotesk family does both the condensed headlines and the body, its width axis set per role.
Status is stated, never implied: every build carries a plain status line (pre-release, sample, running).

regions.label: cut-out featured build (Notifly / rig) on cobalt field

options.label: Photographer's Proof Sheet
options.lineage: darkroom contact sheets: rows of frames, grease-pencil selects, edge numbers
options.thesis: Proof, literally: every project is a roll of frames, the shareable ones circled, the sealed ones fogged.
options.viewport: A contact sheet of the career: a circled frame for Notifly, one for the homelab, fogged frames marked as NDA work, Email in grease pencil.
options.risk: Contact-sheet portfolios are a familiar photographer trope, and it can make the site read as a photography portfolio.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.lineage: museum provenance records: custody lines, dealer stamps, known and inferred passages
options.thesis: A career since 2017 as one custody ribbon: shown work solid, NDA passages in hairline, never faked.
options.viewport: The ribbon enters at 2017 and runs down the page, splitting into sealed work, Notifly, and the homelab.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the NDA gaps are the honest centerpiece) but loses audience identification: museum archives are not this audience's world, and the palette sits in the cream, red, and serif rut.
options.risk: Reads as a heritage brand rather than an engineer, and lands in the most common AI look.

options.label: Designers Republic Sleeve
options.lineage: The Designers Republic record sleeves and Wipeout packaging
options.thesis: Hostile-brand info noise as immaculate branding.
options.viewport: One enormous condensed word shouting through barcode and warning-glyph noise.
options.case: Loses both axes: hiring visitors cannot find the offer in the noise, and its faux-kanji ornament is a costume this owner should not wear.
options.kept: Flat ink edge to edge, no gradients.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Homelab services as a row of ballistic needles.
options.viewport: A row of meters reading Proxmox, Immich, n8n, Beszel.
options.case: Loses both axes: it carries only the homelab and turns the page into an instrument costume.
options.kept: One color reserved for one job.

options.label: Massin Stage Page
options.thesis: Case studies staged as dialogue between constraint and engineer.
options.viewport: Two voices argue across the gutter in colliding sizes.
options.case: Loses both axes: theatrical dialogue confuses a skim-reading hiring visitor.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: The portfolio as an interactive specimen of its own face.
options.viewport: One giant glyph morphing under a weight slider.
options.case: Loses both axes: it proves type taste, not engineering.
options.kept: One variable family, axis set per role.

options.label: Pickling Brine Calendar
options.thesis: Projects as jars maturing on a shelf.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to this audience or product.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The senior developer portfolio as the category ships it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role headline, short intro, Email button, selected work below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev portfolio by design.
